headline: High-risk orchestration pair: LangGraph’s broad write/network defaults can amplify unsafe outputs into actions, while the knowledge-only partner adds little containment.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no I/O surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, so a manual copy-paste or file bridge could still carry injected content into B, but the pathway is unusual and limited by A’s non-executable nature.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-generated text into B’s prompt or files, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to parse untrusted file or stdin content as instructions, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of raw A outputs into B prompts.
Add a fixed instruction prefix/suffix around any pasted content.
Review B prompts for delimiter-based prompt injection handling.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all A outputs before B consumes them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B reads files, writes files, and has broad network egress to model providers and developer-defined tools. If A’s outputs are placed in B’s shared workspace, B can transmit them off-box by default. The pair therefore creates a default leakage path from shared artifacts into B’s backend/tool calls.
conditions: IF A outputs are stored in a filesystem that B can read, B can exfiltrate them via network egress.
IF the shared workspace contains secrets or API keys, B may include them in model-provider or tool traffic.
mitigations: Store A outputs outside B-readable paths.
Restrict B network egress to approved endpoints.
Redact secrets before placing artifacts in shared storage.
Use separate credentials for B’s model-provider calls.
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls between A and B.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B can write the filesystem, execute shells, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress, while its concurrency model explicitly supports multiple instances with shared state via a checkpointer store. That creates a real conflict surface if multiple B instances or external writers touch the same graph state.
conditions: IF two B instances share the same checkpointer store, concurrent writes can race.
IF A-derived artifacts are written into B-managed state, B may overwrite or reorder them.
mitigations: Assign each B invocation a unique state namespace.
Lock shared checkpointer rows during writes.
Avoid writing A artifacts into B-managed state.
Run only one B writer per shared store.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency/version checks to the checkpointer.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a stateful orchestration framework that can route node outputs into downstream actions, while A is a knowledge-management source that can supply content for B to render or act on. Because B’s tool-use pattern is developer-wired and not self-isolating, A’s output can become authoritative input unless the operator adds explicit verification.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text as node input without verification, errors can cascade.
IF B is wired to send emails, commit code, or call APIs from A-derived facts, downstream harm increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any B action node.
Require citations for all A-derived claims.
Separate retrieval nodes from action nodes in B.
Log and diff A inputs before execution.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A-to-B handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for A, and B only states that it handles graph state and model-provider API keys. The pair therefore shows only a generic compliance gap: B’s broad network and state handling could expose data if the operator places regulated content into shared graph state, but the profiles do not prove a concrete violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in B graph state and sent to external model providers, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the operator routes EU or PHI data through B without a documented policy, a mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B graph state.
Document retention and deletion rules for shared state.
Use region-appropriate model endpoints.
Review whether secrets are stored in checkpointer backups.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
